clue.text: Place associated with fever, dreaded disease

parts.note: PL is the standard abbreviation for place, as in street addresses
ague is an old word for a malarial fever with shivering fits

explanation.surface: A location linked with outbreaks of fever is home to a feared illness.
explanation.definitionFit: The bubonic pestilence of history is the archetypal feared epidemic illness.

clue.text: Odd lad taking one name — not this one!

definitions.text: Odd lad taking one name — not this one!

indicators.note: odd suggests something strange or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A strange boy picks up a name, then the setter adds that it is not his.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' scrambles LAD with I and N into a girl's name; the exclamation 'not this one!' says the name is no lad's, so the whole clue both builds and defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, which is exactly what an odd lad could not be called.

clue.text: Loads sing off key in accordance with musical instruction

indicators.note: singing off key means the notes come out wrong, so the letters here are jumbled

explanation.surface: A singer belts out tunes badly while trying to follow the score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in accordance with' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A direction on a score telling the player to slide rapidly up or down the scale.

clue.text: Prophet, man about to encompass jail break?

indicators.note: to encompass something is to surround it, so one piece goes around the other
about here signals that the word is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: he is the pronoun standing for a man

indicators.note: a jail break suggests the letters of jail breaking out of order

explanation.surface: A holy man is about to be locked up, prompting talk of an escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns HE into EH, and 'break' scrambles JAIL into LIJA, which 'to encompass' puts inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament seer who was taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire.

clue.text: Sensational drink's followed by a natural response

indicators.note: followed by places the following pieces after the drink in the answer

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits; the 's stands for is
a tic is an involuntary twitch, a reflex response

explanation.surface: A thrilling drink leaves the taster twitching involuntarily.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking and theatrical, as in a dramatic turn of events.

clue.text: Mechanism for counting on one's fingers?

definitions.text: Mechanism for counting on one's fingers?

parts.words: Mechanism for counting on one's fingers?
parts.note: fingers are digits, so a counting machine that works on digits is the electronic kind that handles numbers in binary

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a child counting on their hands; the cryptic reading takes 'fingers' as digits, the 0s and 1s a calculating machine processes.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic calculating machine that handles data as discrete numeric values.

clue.text: What may happen given no restraint in a night going around New York?

definitions.text: What may happen given no restraint

indicators.note: around places the rearranged letters on both sides of the other piece
going here means going wrong, so the letters of a night are rearranged

explanation.surface: A night out on the town in New York with no limits at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' scrambles A NIGHT into ANTHIG, and 'around' wraps it round NY; the definition echoes 'anything goes'.
explanation.definitionFit: When nothing is restricted, every outcome is possible: anything goes.

clue.text: Include article about curious upset

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article goes round the other piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: odd means strange or curious

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put in a piece about an odd disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ODD into DDO, which 'about' puts inside AN.
explanation.definitionFit: To append or attach something extra to what is already there.

clue.text: Pressure to get ventilation pipe installed in pub by civil engineer

indicators.note: installed in means put inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a flue is a duct carrying smoke or air out of a building

explanation.surface: A builder pushes to have a chimney duct fitted in a local bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Influence is sway or persuasive power exerted on someone, a kind of pressure.

clue.text: Popular little woman itching to behave thus?

definitions.text: Popular little woman itching to behave thus?

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Vi is a short form of the woman's name Violet
tingly means prickling or itching with excitement

explanation.surface: A well-liked young woman is eager to act in a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a popular girl eager for attention would behave in an alluring way.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in an alluring or tempting manner, as a sought-after girl itching for company might.

clue.text: Flower commonly starts to droop after February first

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of each of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A bloom begins to wilt once February has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' says the definition is a dialect or informal word: a daff is a daffodil in everyday British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal, regional shortening of daffodil, the yellow spring bloom.

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a hag is an ugly or unpleasant old woman
up as in up in arms, in revolt

explanation.surface: An unpleasant old crone in rebellion is caring for a psychological block.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis or emotional block, an informal term for a psychological fixation.

clue.text: A French mate Desmond backed, nem con

parts.note: un is the French for a
oppo is British slang for a friend or colleague

indicators.note: in a down clue backed means turned back, read the other way

parts.note: Des is the short form of Desmond

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's friend supported Desmond without dissent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns DES into SED. Nem con is Latin shorthand for unanimously, with no one objecting.
explanation.definitionFit: Nem con means with no one against, so a motion passed that way met no opposition.

clue.text: Arabs destroy weeds — a sign of luck?

parts.note: Arabs are a breed of horse
to hoe is to cut down weeds with a garden tool

explanation.surface: Arab people wiping out weeds may be seen as a good omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arabs' looks like people, but it is the breed of horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved iron hoof plate, hung over doors as a traditional good-fortune charm.

clue.text: Speaking in tongues not for one such?

definitions.text: Speaking in tongues not for one such?

parts.words: Speaking in tongues not for one such?
parts.note: speaking in tongues plural is beyond a person who has command of only a single language

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests religious glossolalia; the cryptic sense is speaking several languages, impossible for someone limited to one.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who knows just a single language, the opposite of a polyglot.

clue.text: Sad daughter needs a sherry

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies
oloroso is a dark, full-bodied type of sherry

explanation.surface: A gloomy girl needs a glass of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is only a link. The definition is the Italian musical direction for sorrowfully.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning to play in a sorrowful, mournful manner.

clue.text: King's shriek of surprise at smell

parts.note: R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king; the 's is a link
eek is a cry of alarm or surprise

explanation.surface: A monarch cries out in shock at a nasty odour.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong, unpleasant stench or stink.

clue.text: If not cloudy, characterised by absence of sun?

indicators.note: absence of means the named letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a cloudy sky is sunless

explanation.surface: A forecaster's conditional remark about an overcast day without sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characterised by absence of' removes S from SUNLESS, the synonym of 'cloudy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjunction meaning except on condition that, i.e. if it is not the case.

clue.text: Old piece of legislation is precise

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
an act is a law passed by parliament

explanation.surface: A former law is described as exact in its wording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is just a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate and correct in every detail.

clue.text: Game for children, running through Memphis pyramids

indicators.note: running through means the answer runs across the following words inside them

explanation.surface: A children's guessing game played among the pyramids of ancient Memphis.
explanation.definitionFit: A guessing game where one player names an initial letter of something seen.

clue.text: Put address on this for Consignia boss?

definitions.text: Put address on this for Consignia boss?

parts.words: Put address on this for Consignia boss?
parts.note: Consignia was the short-lived name of the British Royal Mail, so its boss is the chief of the post, and printed stationery carries a sender's address

explanation.walkthrough: Consignia was the name Britain's Post Office briefly took in 2001; its boss heads the mail, while the stationery top carries your address.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed notepaper heading showing the sender's name and address; punningly, the chief of the post.

clue.text: One reverencing image inordinately? One joins party afterwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a do is a party or celebration
later means afterwards

explanation.surface: A worshipper of a statue comes along to a party later on.
explanation.definitionFit: A worshipper of false gods or graven figures, or anyone who admires something to excess.

clue.text: Treated steel keeps very graceful

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
treated metal has been processed and changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Specially treated steel stays very elegant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated' scrambles STEEL into SELTE, which 'keeps' V inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender and elegant in figure, slim in a stylish way.
